purpose: Narrow DELIVERY successor for the bundled Rust semantic-provider child: exact cardinality, lifecycle, launch, supervision and conditional D9 v1.13 fate. It does not edit or silently amend delivery.v2.json.

dependencyPins.use: existing sidecar, offline-bundle, platform and termination-integration authority
exact proposed D9 successor vocabulary and derivation
independent pre-freeze review of the exact D9 v1.13 candidate bytes

protocolReference.applicationRule: This join becomes usable only when the protocol artifact, this join, the resolved-inputs join and their retained checker are independently reviewed and formally applied together. A filename or matching field is not application authority.

keyFields: complete closed resolved-inputs rust-v1 semantic-universe value
workerCardinality.keyComparison: Exact recursive value equality after the host validates the closed rust-v1 record; no digest-only comparison, prefix, providerVersion-only comparison or implementation-local cache key may replace it.

processModel.start: After the AttemptRecord, sealed Snapshot, verified PlanId, selected rust-v1 universe, exact repository-resolution projection and admitted Rust semantic stages exist, start exactly one child immediately before the first admitted rust-semantic stage for the key. Starting during request validation, PlanIntent construction, snapshot capture or PlanId construction is forbidden.
processModel.stageSharing: One Analyze carries all and only admitted C-2 fact-derivation stages with operator=semantic-provider and providerId=rust-semantic for this exact key, in verified ExecutionPlan stage order. No stage from another key or provider is sent.
processModel.end: After any valid terminal plus required process fate, user cancellation, protocol fault, process fault or delivery failure, close pipes, terminate the child process group/job if still live, reap every descendant owned by the child, delete private scratch and forget all compiler/provider state before returning from the supervisor.
processModel.tcbPosture: The provider, pinned compiler and any explicitly granted pre-Plan repository-resolution tools are TCB-accepted. Process separation contains crashes and compiler instability; it is not a security sandbox and grants no capability-confinement claim.
processModel.pureCoreExclusion: The child and supervisor remain outside the lifetime-neutral pure core.

ownership.repositoryExecutionOwner: The host resolved-inputs adapter, after snapshot seal and before PlanId construction, owns any explicitly granted build-script/procedural-macro execution. It seals outputs and logical tool-path descriptors into PlanId inputs, terminates that preparation activity, and only then may the semantic child start.

launch.executable: Absolute digest-verified path of the signed rust-provider artifact selected by the release manifest; no PATH lookup or shell.
launch.argvRule: The six command-array elements above are exact and ordered. Placeholder values are host-resolved absolute paths; no additional argument, response file, shell expansion or project-controlled argument is allowed.

stdio.stdin: new inherited unidirectional pipe, host writes protocol frames only
stdio.stdout: new inherited unidirectional pipe, protocol frames only from process start through EOF
stdio.stderr: new inherited byte pipe, diagnostic-only and never parsed as authority

roots.toolchainRoot: Read-only verified extraction of rust-toolchain-bundle; every selected component stays beneath this root and matches the signed artifact bytes.
roots.scratchRoot: Fresh private host-owned directory for this child only, bounded by protocol limits, never evidence or cache authority, removed at end.
roots.snapshot: Transferred only by the protocol sealed-VFS frames; no live worktree or repository root is passed.

preSpawnChecks: selected profile contains rust-provider and rust-toolchain-bundle
artifact digests and dependency edges match the signed release
platformId is one of DELIVERY's five supported rows
provider executable and toolchain root are absolute and contained in their verified installations
private scratch exists with restrictive host-selected permissions
no system rustc, Cargo, sysroot, loader, linker or PATH substitution is selected

diagnosticsAndScratchBounds.stderrOverflow: Capture the first maxStderrBytes, append a host-owned truncation marker outside provider bytes, and continue protocol validation; stderr alone never changes semantic or D9 fate.
diagnosticsAndScratchBounds.scratchOverflow: Terminate and reap the child, discard candidates and map provider-protocol / PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

d9Reference.rule: The mappings below use only values present in the exact D9 v1.13 candidate. The independent review makes those candidate bytes acceptable for pre-freeze reference; it does not apply v1.13 to DELIVERY, this join or any product. Until formal application, current DELIVERY's v1.6 reference remains current and no implementation may silently substitute v1.13.

supervisorEventMap.d9Projection: No provider deficiency or fault is introduced; final D9 class remains derived from the complete host finalization state.
class=interrupted; exitCode=130; no reasonCode or errorCode
class=interrupted; exitCode=130; the user signal is not overwritten by provider-protocol

exhaustivenessRule: Every child outcome is classified by exactly one row after applying D9 interruption precedence. An implementation-local exit status, private provider error spelling, partial Coverage seal or timeout-as-budget rule is forbidden.
residuals: Formal application to DELIVERY and formal application of D9 v1.13 are outside this candidate.
Independent review must replay every event row and dependency hash before application.
Product implementation, descendant-process behavior, network-disabled repository preparation, platform qualification and release evidence remain unexecuted.
